## Target context
- Repo: DontPanic

- Project: (none)

[F003] The command works end-to-end on a real plan, exit-coding 1 because block-severity flags are present, and renders the F001 flags plus F002 split proposals from one typed source. Done.

## Summary

I implemented F003, the `dontpanic plan-review <plan> [--format text|json]` CLI surface. I added a new pure module `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/plan_review/report.py` that assembles a single typed `PlanScopeReport` (running the F001 lint over every feature and the F002 split proposer over each) and renders both the human `text` and machine `json` views from that one source — `build_plan_scope_report` does no I/O and mutates nothing, so the command is read-only. I wired a thin `_plan_review_main` handler into `cli.py` (resolves the plan, loads it, builds resolvers from the live CLI grammar + package module names, prints the report, and returns exit 1 iff any block-severity flag exists, else 0), and registered `plan-review` in `command_validation._VOCABULARY` (plus a new public `known_flags()` helper) and in `agent_manifest`'s `supported_commands`. I added `test_plan_review_cli_f003.py` (7 tests) covering text output, json output, the non-zero-on-block exit, a clean-plan zero-flag exit, the read-only invariant, token-shape validation, and manifest membership; I also updated the pinned `known_subcommands` set in `test_command_validation_f001.py`. All 162 targeted tests across the affected files pass, and a dogfood run against the real plan produced the expected BLOCK report with exit
